title: QBR Commitment Catalogue + Stakeholder Roles Sprint
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, operational-first QBR runbook focused on producing a clean, prioritized set of customer commitments (the 'Commitment Catalogue') and a clear owner/communications plan. Goal is to leave every QBR with 3–6 named commitments, a single owner for each, measurable success criteria, and an explicit 30/60/90 follow-up cadence.

Intended audience:
- CSMs running enterprise QBRs
- Solutions/SEs who support technical commitments
- AMs and renewal owners

When to use:
- Strategic accounts where renewal is within 6–12 months OR usage/cost signals show variance
- Mid-quarter mini-QBRs focused on risk/commitments

Run of show (45–60m compact):
1) 00:00–05:00 — Welcome + agenda + updated success metric snapshot (CSM, brief)
2) 05:00–15:00 — Health & adoption signals + critical risks (data-driven, show 1–2 charts)
3) 15:00–25:00 — Product/technical blockers + proposed mitigations (SE owns)
4) 25:00–40:00 — Commitment sprint: surface candidate actions, prioritize, assign owners
5) 40:00–50:00 — Commitment confirmation and dates; set follow-up cadence
6) 50:00–60:00 — Executive asks & close (next review date, renewal check-in trigger)

Facilitator script (short prompts you can read):
- Intro: "Thanks everyone for joining. Our goal today is to align on the top actions that will materially reduce renewal risk and drive value in the next 90 days. We'll capture commitments, assign owners, and confirm dates so we can track progress."
- Health to Risk transition: "Quick snapshot — three things that matter from our POV: adoption, cost, and ROI. If any of these are red, we pause and capture specific mitigation commitments."
- When running the commitment sprint: "We will rapid-fire candidate commitments for 8 minutes. Aim for small, testable outcomes with a clear owner. Avoid open-ended asks — convert ideas into 'owner + deliverable + date'."
- Closing commitments: "Can each owner confirm they accept the deliverable and the date? If not, propose alternate due date now so we can set realistic expectations."

Commitment Catalogue template (plain text table you can paste into notes):
Commitment ID | Short description | Owner | Due date | Impact (why it matters) | Success metric | Follow-up cadence | Current status
C-1 | Migrate 5 pilot users to new routing | Carlos Rivera | 2026-01-15 | Reduce latency complaints for pilot by 60% | #pilot users on new routing = 5 | Weekly sync until complete | Draft
C-2 | Enable prefix KV cache for top 3 endpoints | Priya Kapoor | 2025-12-20 | Lower token cost per request by 12% | Cost per 1k tokens decreased by 12% | Bi-weekly check-in | Draft

How to prioritize commitments quickly (tiebreaker rubric):
- Likelihood to materially change renewal outcome (High/Medium/Low)
- Effort (S/M/L) — if large, require milestone breakdown
- Measurable success criteria present (Yes/No)
- Owner availability (Green/Amber/Red)
Pick first by High likelihood + Small/Medium effort.

Preflight checklist (send 48h before):
- Confirm deck has a one-slide 'current state' with 3 metrics (usage, cost, satisfaction)
- Invite technical SE for any commitment that touches infra or configuration
- Share a one-paragraph desired outcome (what we want the customer to agree to)
- Ask customer to pre-seed 1 pain point and 1 desired outcome in the calendar invite
- Prepare the Commitment Catalogue live doc and a follow-up email template

Post-meeting deliverables (within 24–48h):
- Email to attendees with: 1) confirmed commitments table, 2) owners and dates, 3) next check-in date and cadence
- Create JIRA/Asana tasks for commitments that require engineering work; link back in the table
- Add follow-up items to CSM's tracking sheet and update account health score

30/60/90-day follow-up plan (encode in calendar and ops):
- 30d: Quick status snapshot (CSM) — red/yellow/green; update success metric
- 60d: Demo of progress or interim results (SE + CSM)
- 90d: Outcome review + renewal signal update (AM + CSM + Exec sponsor)

Red flags and immediate escalation ladder:
- "Owner drops": If an owner drops a commitment, escalate to CSM lead within 48h and propose replacement
- "No measurable success metric": Pause commitment, rework into smaller measurable milestone
- "Blocked by engineering backlog": Create a ticket, tag SRE/Infra lead, include proposed rollback/fallback plan
Escalation contacts: Priority escalation path: CSM -> AM -> Solutions Lead -> Head of Customer Success

Suggested slide order for the meeting deck (minimal):
1) Cover + desired outcome
2) Current state snapshot (3 metrics)
3) Top 3 risks and impact
4) Technical blockers & proposed fixes
5) Commitment sprint frame + live Commitment Catalogue
6) Confirmed commitments and next steps

One-paragraph follow-up email template (send ASAP):
Subject: Follow-up: QBR outcomes and agreed commitments (Account: {{account_name}})
Hi {{primary_contact}},
Thanks for your time today. As discussed, below are the commitments we confirmed and the owners/dates. We will check in on day 30 with a short status update and demo at day 60. Please flag if anything looks off.
[Insert Commitment Catalogue table]
Best,
{{CSM name}}

Quick facilitation notes (notes-to-self):
- If the customer requests scope creep, convert to a new candidate commitment and deprioritize unless it moves renewal needle
- Keep execs on time: use the last 10m for their ask only; give them a single slide to present
- Use JIRA IDs in the table to avoid losing action items in email threads

Examples of good commitments (for coaching):
- "CSM to deliver 2-week onboarding plan for new workflow, owner: Priya Kapoor, due 2025-12-05, success: 80% of pilot users complete onboarding."
- "SE to validate API config and deploy patch to staging, owner: Mai Nguyen, due 2025-11-28, success: staging e2e tests pass and latency < 150ms."

Open questions / follow-ups for this doc:
- Should we add a standard SLA-for-commitments template for engineering-backed items?
- Can we automate a daily JIRA -> Commitment Catalogue sync? (Ping infra tooling team)

End of doc.
